Below is what an AI scientist wrote during a search in that world: its analysis at every round, in order, and the
name and hypothesis of the trial it ended with. Does the text, anywhere, state the rule?
- "yes": it states the rule's substance (what is changed and how).
- "partly": it identifies the right kind of change but not its specifics.
- "no": anything else.

## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no trials yet, and the starting architecture scored 0.000 on both seeds. The default recipe makes only 32 PPO updates of 4,096 samples each, which is probably too few for a task that needs 6-16 error-free placements followed by a correctly timed DONE. Fewer PPO epochs buy more samples: 1.86x the steps at 2 epochs and 3.25x at 1 epoch. Smaller rollouts also give more frequent updates. Two candidates keep the starting network and change only the recipe, to see whether the recipe alone unlocks learning. The third tests a new idea: a head that scores each placement at each layer, so that 'all footprint cells missing at the landing layer' becomes a simple pool over the footprint. It stays under the starting network's FLOPs, so it uses the same recipe as candidate 1 and keeps the same sample count.

### Round 2
Every trial scored exactly 0, both on dev and on training success in the last 10% of training. That includes three different setups: 1 or 2 PPO epochs, 231k to 405k steps, and a per-layer head. Since there is no signal at all, small recipe changes are unlikely to explain the gap. A deeper mismatch is more likely. The note says the world may differ from the description. One possibility is that the action layout is not the (type, y, x) top-left layout the conv heads assume, for example transposed or anchored at a different corner. If so, a translation-equivariant conv head cannot line its scores up with the real placements. This round tests that with heads that can map positions arbitrarily: a conv trunk plus a dense head, a transformer with learned positional embeddings, and a plain MLP that makes no layout assumption. If all three stay at 0, the cause is more likely reward or exploration, for example the agent collapsing to an early DONE, than network structure.

### Round 3
All six trials scored exactly 0 on both seeds, and none had any training success either. They covered two recipes, a per-layer head, a dense remap head, a transformer and an MLP. Recipe changes (1 or 2 epochs, up to 405k steps) did nothing. The starting pool head was presumably designed to work on the world as described, so a flat 0 suggests the world breaks one of its built-in assumptions. Likely suspects are the anchor corner, the brick orientation (dy,dx), the brick-type order, or a transposed (x-major) action index. The MLP and transformer don't assume a layout but are weak learners for this budget, so their 0 says little against this idea. This round hedges directly. Two candidates use a head that pools over every footprint orientation and anchor corner and also outputs a transposed logit map, one per recipe. The third uses learned per-action queries that attend to the conv cell features, so it assumes no layout at all.

### Round 4
All nine trials scored 0 on dev. Training success in the last 10% of training was also 0 for every trial. This held for conv nets, the per-layer head, the transformer, the layout-agnostic MLP, the robust bank head and the action-query attention. Because even the MLP got nothing, a mismatch between the network and the action or observation layout is unlikely to be the only cause. The more likely cause is optimisation: exact builds need every placement right plus a well-timed DONE. With default-style recipes the policy probably stays too random, or too short-sighted with gamma 0.95, to reach the +1 terminal bonus. Recipe settings untested so far: low entropy, higher gamma and lambda, a higher learning rate with large minibatches, and many small updates. In this final round two trials test recipe changes on the starting network, and one tests a head that also receives a learned linear projection of the raw observation, under the same recipe as the first.
